column1: # The names a catalogue index keeps, and which decoders open each one.
# **One list, read by both runtimes.** The phone's copy is
# moment the two disagree, so a name added on one side and not the other cannot ship. The page reads
# this file at run time and keeps a name only if **at least one of its decoders is in the engine it
# is running on** -- which is how the browser, whose build has no ZXTune, comes to index 61% of
# Modland rather than all of it.
# A decoder is judged absent only when the engine says so: `pt_backends` ends in `zxtune:none` when
# that decoder is compiled out, and names nothing else as missing. HivelyTracker is in every build
# and is not in the fingerprint at all, so "not mentioned" must mean "present" -- the rule is the
# engine's absence, never this file's guess.
# Two names have two decoders, and that is not a mistake: `fc` is the Amiga Future Composer to
# libopenmpt and an Atari 8-bit format to ASAP; `psm` is Epic MegaGames to libopenmpt and Pro Sound
# Maker to ZXTune. Either decoder being present keeps the name.
# The fourth column is the machine a name belongs to -- `Platforms.forFileName` on the phone, which
# the dock names beside the author ("Jogeir Liljedahl · Amiga · 1994"). The same test holds it to the
# phone's table; `-` is a name no platform claims.
# ZX Spectrum -- the rows the browser build cannot open
# The Amiga custom formats, through UADE. The phone's alone: UADE is a second process and
# WebAssembly cannot start one, so the page's engine says `uade:none` and these rows drop out of
# its index. Measured in `SupportedFormats`, which says which Modland directory each came from.
# Filename prefixes, the Amiga way: `mod.title` rather than `title.mod`
# Directories whose files nothing here plays, whatever their names say (`docs/STATUS.md` C88).
# The index decides by name, and these names belong to another format: Deflemask's `.dmf` is read
# by libopenmpt as X-Tracker's DMF, FamiTracker's `.ftm` as Face The Music, and Music Editor's old
# `.med` is not the OctaMED MMD it expects. None of 20 sampled from each opened in the page, and the
# owner found none that played on the phone either (2026-09-23): 3,718 files offered and refused.
# Their rows stay in the index, unoffered, and a decoder that learns one of them is a line removed
# here. SidMon 1's `.sid` is not listed: the phone plays it, through UADE.
